acceptanceCriteria.text: Add one canonical operation-book document under `docs/` and mark it as the chronological execution authority for the Route 4 -> Route 1 deployment/convergence sequence.
Enumerate every operation in strict execution order with stable step IDs; no route may be represented only by a prose summary.

Every step records trigger/preconditions, purpose, owner, input authority, exact action, state read/mutation, output/evidence, fail-closed conditions, recovery/idempotency semantics, and next handoff condition.

Explicitly distinguish **release identity authority**, **host bootstrap authority**, **provider lifecycle authority (Lima)**, **QEMU external toolchain identity**, **canonical NixOS guest authority**, **managed-generation authority**, and **Route 1 payload authority**; no step may silently create a second authority.

Declare every external host prerequisite actually consumed by the selected provider path; ambient PATH/HOME state is either prohibited, explicitly validated, or explicitly part of the supported precondition.
Describe all durable state/provenance written under the host-bootstrap state root and identify which later steps consume each record.
Describe credential/key lifecycle, including first creation, guest delivery, persistence, host restart, key loss/drift, and existing-instance behavior.
Describe all reconciliation branches: missing, satisfied/no-op, stopped-compatible, repairable interrupted state, incompatible, ambiguous, and unsupported.

Map each operation/handoff to its current implementation entrypoint(s) and existing proof tier: unit/hermetic PR proof, trusted-main canonical integration, release certification, or #261 external real-host certification.
Include an explicit coverage/gap matrix that references at least #826, #840, #841, #842, #843, #844, #845, #846, #847, and #261 at the exact affected operation steps.
Any newly discovered missing operation, producer/consumer connection, undeclared dependency, or absent proof is filed as a focused follow-up Issue rather than silently described as implemented.
Existing deployment/host-bootstrap/Lima Runtime documentation links to the operation book instead of independently restating a competing end-to-end sequence.
The document clearly separates current implemented behavior from target behavior where an open defect still blocks the target chain.

The operation book contains a compact end-to-end sequence diagram/table that can be reviewed top-to-bottom without consulting code, while detailed entries retain exact implementation/evidence references.

issue.title: chore: define the complete Route 4 to Route 1 operation book
